evidence.note: Wrote a reusable WS+IRC integration test, inspected raw IRC registration numerics, found a discrepancy, fixed it, and re-ran — direct socket-level protocol verification with self-correction.
Built resilience.js that actively SIGKILLs an HTTP node AND kills the bus (broadcast component) — reproduces both grader failure-injection scenarios rather than assuming resilience works.
Verified SPA testids, installed Chromium/Playwright, and ran a browser end-to-end UI pass (ui.py) against the pinned semantic elements.
Exercised error-code invariants across subsystems: role permissions, mention edge cases, 413/topic-length/404/401 — verifying negative paths, not just happy paths.

Re-ran all suites (smoke, ws/irc, ui, resilience) on a fresh clean-DB instance and verified WS head_seq + resume replay semantics across all three nodes — re-verification after changes rather than trusting prior passes.

reasoning: The agent built reusable checks spanning all four transports (REST smoke.sh, ws_irc.js, resilience.js, ui.py), verified key invariants directly (head_seq, resume replay, cross-node behavior, error codes), and — critically — actively killed both an HTTP node and the broadcast bus to confirm continued operation, which is exactly the level-8 anchor. It also touches level-10 behaviors (browser pass against pinned testids, failures driving fixes, fresh-instance re-verification), but I see no explicit exactly-once fan-out assertion or node-restart-within-60s recovery check, so it does not fully reach 10.
